Which one of the following was the immediate cause of the First Carnatic War?
o: Capture of French ships by the British
x: The First Carnatic War (1746-48 A.D.) was an offshoot of the Anglo-French rivalry in the Austrian War of succession that took place in Europe in 1740 AD. The British Commodore Bernett captured some French ships which became the immediate cause of the war. Nawab Anwaruddin sent an army under the command of Mahfooz Khan to besiege the French in Madras during the first Carnatic War. The French Army (under the command of Captain Paradise) defeated Nawab’s Army at the Battle of St. Thome near Adyar river. Treaty of Aix-La-Chapelle (18 Oct, 1748 A.D.) ended the War of Austrian succession and with it first Carnatic War ended and the Britishers reoccupied Madras. The first Carnatic War is memorable for the War of St. Thome.

s: Who was the Nawab of Bengal when the Battle of Buxar was fought?
x: On 22/23 October, 1764 A.D. British Army defeated allied forces of Mir Qasim, Nawab of Oudh Shuja-ud-Daula and Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. British Army’s command was in the hands of Major Hector Munro in the Battle of Buxar. The battle of Buxar assured the result of Plassey battle and established British supremacy on Banaras and Allahabad (Prayagraj) across the Ganges. The battle of Buxar made way for British and proved that there was no strong competitor before the British. The battle of Buxar completed what Plassey had begun. During the battle of Buxar Nawab of Bengal was Mir Jafar. According to Sir James Stephen, ‘’The battle of Buxar deserves more credit than the battle of Plassey as the origin of British power in India”. If the results of both significant battles are analyzed, it can be said that the battle of Plassey was won by treachery, but the battle of Buxar showed the supremacy of English armies and military skills. Plassey made the English the only controllers of Bengal while Buxar raised the political prestige of the Company throughout India.

x: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) was fought between the French forces and the British East India Company during the Carnatic Wars, leading to the decline of French power in India. The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought between the British East India Company, led by Hector Munro, and the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula, and Shah Alam II, not between Mir Jafar and Clive. The Battle of Chilianwala (1849) was fought during the Second Anglo-Sikh War, not between Dalhousie and the Marathas. The Battle of Kharda (1795) was fought between the Nizam of Hyderabad and the Marathas, not the East India Company.

s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the battles fought in India in the 18 th Century?
o: Battle of Wandiwash – Battle of Buxar – Battle of Ambur – Battle of Plassey
Battle of Ambur – Battle of Plassey – Battle of Wandiwash – Battle of Buxar
Battle of Wandiwash – Battle of Plassey – Battle of Ambur – Battle of Buxar
Battle of Ambur – Battle of Buxar – Battle of Wandiwash – Battle of Plassey
x: The correct chronological order is Battle of Ambur (1749), Battle of Plassey (1757), Battle of Wandiwash (1760), and Battle of Buxar (1764). The Battle of Ambur was fought during the Second Carnatic War and marked the beginning of intense Anglo-French rivalry in South India. The Battle of Plassey established British political influence in Bengal. The Battle of Wandiwash decisively ended French ambitions in India by securing British supremacy in the Carnatic region. Finally, the Battle of Buxar consolidated British power in northern India and paved the way for the grant of Diwani rights in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.

s: Which one of the following rulers had granted Diwani to the East India Company?
x: As per the first Treaty of Allahabad (August 1765 A.D.), the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II was taken under the Company’s protection and was to reside at Allahabad. The Emperor issued an order dated 12th August, 1765 granting Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. During this time Robert Clive was Governor of East India Company in Bengal. The emperor’s order legalized the political authority of Company in Bengal and British rule expanded all over India including Delhi. Successors of Shah Alam II i.e. Akbar II (1806-37 A.D.) and Bahadurshah II (1837-57 A.D.) became pensioners of East India Company.

s: Who was appointed Deputy Diwan of Murshidabad by Robert Clive after the Allahabad Treaty?
x: According to the Treaty of Allahabad (August, 1765 A.D.), Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II was taken under the Company’s protection and had to reside at Allahabad. Shah Alam II conferred Diwani (fiscal revenue collection authority) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the Company by issuing ‘Farman’ on 12 August, 1765 A.D. Nazm-ud-duala (son of Mir Jafar) was accepted as Nawab of Bengal. In return, the company had to pay the emperor an annual sum of Rs 26 Lakhs as pension. At that time, the Company was neither interested in taking responsibility for tax revenue collection nor was it capable of doing so. Therefore, the Company appointed two Diwans- Mohammad Raza Khan for Bengal and Raja Shitab Rai for Bihar. Thus, all business of Diwani and Nizamat was conducted by Indians but authorized by the British Company.

s: Which one of the following is an important historical novel written during the latter half of the nineteenth century?
x: Durgeshnandini (also written as Durgesh Nandini) is a Bengali historical romance novel authored by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and first published in 1865. It is clearly characterised as a historical novel set against the backdrop of the Pathan–Mughal conflicts during Akbar's reign. His notable works, including Anandamath (1882), Kapalkundala (1866), and Devi Chaudhurani (1884), reflect the social, cultural, and moral concerns of a colonised society striving for self-identity. Nibandhmala (Garland of Essays) is a historically significant Marathi periodical launched by nationalist writer Vishnushastri Chiplunkar in 1874 to foster pride in Swarajya, Swadharm, and Swabhasha. s: Englishmen made the Treaty of Srirangapatna with–
x: Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92 A.D.) ended with the Treaty of Srirangapatna (1792 A.D.). The treaty of Seringapatam (Srirangapatna) was signed in March 1792 A.D. between Tipu Sultan of Mysore and Lord Cornwallis on behalf of British East India Company. The agreement also included representative of the Nizam of Hyderabad and Maratha Empire, requiring Tipu to Cede half of his Kingdom. According to the treaty, Half of the territories of Tipu were snatched away from him and divided among Marathas, British, and Nizam. Tipu had to pay Rs. 330 lakhs as war indemnity to British as his two sons were kept hostage. These was a terms and condition in the treaty that until Tipu wouldn’t provide 3 crore rupees, his two sons will be under British protection.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: First Anglo-Mysore - Haidar Ali was defeated
Second Anglo-Mysore - Haidar Ali defeated the
Third Anglo-Mysore - Tipu Sultan won the
x: (i) First Anglo-Mysore War was held in 1767-1769 A.D. and ended with Treaty of Madras on 4 April, 1769 AD. British Governor of Bengal was Harry Verelst during the war. (ii) Second Anglo-Mysore War was fought in 1780-1784 A.D. and ended with the Treaty of Mangalore. Warren Hastings was the British Governor-General during the war. (iii) Third Anglo-Mysore War occurred in 1790-92 A.D. under commands of Lord Cornwallis and ended with Treaty of Srirangapatna. Tipu requested support from Kustuntunia and France by sending his ambassador but his effort was worthless. (iv) 4th Anglo-Mysore War was fought in 1799 A.D., led by Governor General Lord Wellesley. On 4 May 1799, British annexed Srirangapatna Fort and Tipu got martyrdom in the battle. Family members of Tipu were imprisoned in Vellore.
